09:30 Local Time, 07:30 GMT, 13:00 IST: One Test. One series to be won. And the No. 1 spot in the world up for grabs. South Africa and Australia arrive in Cape Town with everything to play for after trading emphatic victories in the first two Tests. Australia struck first in Durban, but South Africa hit back in Gqeberha, where Temba Bavuma’s magnificent 179 and Marco Jansen’s all-round brilliance turned the contest on its head. Now, with the series locked at 1-1, Newlands will have the final say.

Hello and a warm welcome to what should be a riveting contest between two of the most competitive sides in Test cricket. Australia have plenty to put right after their batting unravelled in the second Test. Cameron Green’s return offers a boost, Matt Renshaw is set to open alongside Travis Head, and Steven Smith’s fitness remains a key talking point after his recent back and neck concerns. Smith also returns to a venue associated with one of the lowest points of his career (sandpaper gate), adding another layer to an already significant occasion. South Africa, meanwhile, have named Gerald Coetzee in place of the injured Anrich Nortje, with the rest of their winning side unchanged. Aiden Markram’s promising starts will need to translate into a substantial score if the hosts are to put Australia under sustained pressure.
Nishchal: "Excited for this clash" -- You're not alone in that

Newlands should provide an intriguing examination of both batting line-ups, with a dry surface carrying some grass and largely sunny weather forecast. South Africa will look to Kagiso Rabada and Jansen to exploit the conditions, while Australia’s experienced pace attack will be eager to expose the vulnerabilities that emerged in Gqeberha. The visitors have a strong overall record at the ground, though recent results offer South Africa reason to believe. With the series and the world No. 1 ranking on the line, there is no room left for a second chance. Pitch report, toss, team details coming up shortly, stay tuned...
